sources.citation: Hogbin, H. Ian. 1930. Notes on a grammar of the language of Ongtong Java. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 5(4): 823-853.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: p.826: 'Accentuation generally falls on the penultimate syllable..' for Ongtong Java (onto1237); Nukumanu is never mentioned, so not applicable to nuku1258.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page nuku1258 (refs: Ray 1919/20; Sarfert & Damm 1929-31; Te kkai te Ista 2003); Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist.
sources.note: n/a (bibliography only; confirms no grammar/phonology reference exists in Glottolog).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1916. Polynesian linguistics III: Polynesian languages of the Solomon Islands. V. The Tasman Islands; VI. A vocabulary of the dialects of Tauu and Nukumanu, by Dr. G. Friederici. Journal of the Polynesian Society 25: 18-23, 99-103.
sources.note: Nukumanu 'Phonology' paragraph (p.101) covers only Lepsius alphabet, r/l interchange and two ch-like sounds; no accent/stress rule. Friederici's word list carries Lepsius accent marks (e.g. teraha 'beard', kametse 'bowl', scanned-garbled); JPS editor's note (p.103) says the accents are largely 'superfluous' and that Friederici 'has accented letters that have no accent or stress'.

sources.citation: Parkinson, R. 1907. Dreissig Jahre in der Suedsee. Stuttgart: Strecker & Schroeder (chapter on Nuguria, Tauu, Nukumanu).
sources.note: Fraktur scanned is poor; no stress/Betonung remark about Nukumanu speech located.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Nukumanu language' (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Short vocabulary with acute-accented forms (niu, 'ulu, huki, kolo, naku, puata, tono, henie) copied from the Suedsee-Expedition volumes; no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Davletshin, Albert. 2014. A seemingly on-going sound change in Takuu language of Papua New Guinea: historical and theoretical implications. Journal of Language Relationship / Voprosy jazykovogo rodstva 12: 1-20.
sources.note: Nukumanu: 'geminated consonants do not have phonemic status in Takuu, Nukeria, Nukumanu and Sikaiana.. In Nukeria, Nukumanu and Sikaiana all single and double consonants show the same quality; acoustically they differ in duration only' (p.8); the poetic [a]->[o] shift 'is attested in Nukumanu (Johnstone, Feinberg 2006)' (p.8); 'According to my Nukumanu consultant (male, about 40 years old), the sound change r -> l is nearing completion in Nukumanu. However, my own Nukumanu wordlist and an unpublished Nukumanu lexicon of 2000 (Feinberg n.d.) show similar distribution patterns for [l] and [r]'…

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (rev. ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics; Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002. The Oceanic languages.
sources.note: Nukumanu appears only in language lists / endangerment remarks; no data source and nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2012. The languages of Melanesia: quantifying the level of coverage. In N. Evans & M. Klamer (eds), Melanesian Languages on the Edge of Asia: Challenges for the 21st Century (LD&C Special Publication 5), 13-34. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press. Online appendix (per-language most-extensive-description list).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: documentation-status record only: most extensive sources listed = Ray 1919/1920 (overview, comparative, wordlist) only; confirms no grammar/phonology existed by 2012; no stress data

sources.citation: Parkinson, Richard. 2010 [1907]. Thirty Years in the South Seas: Land and People, Customs and Traditions in the Bismarck Archipelago and on the German Solomon Islands. Translated by John Dennison; translation edited by J. Peter White. Sydney: Sydney University Press. Chapter 7 'The Eastern Islands (Nuguria, Tauu and Nukumanu)', pp. c.224-246 (doi:10.2307/jj.39704434.17); Chapter 10 'Languages', pp. c.310-340, also checked.
sources.note: No phonology content. The only language passage (p.228): 'I have already mentioned that the languages of these islands show a great similarity, and moreover are very closely related to the central Polynesian languages. Samoan is immediately and without great difficulty understood on the islands; however, closer investigation elicits the fact that many words originate from the north, particularly from the Carolines'. Elsewhere only scattered Nukumanu words (Ba e lagi, makua, umaka, sisio..) without accent marks and the remark that Tauu is 'pronounced Tau'u'u'. Nothing on stress, accent or tone…

sources.citation: Johnstone, Jennifer & Richard Feinberg. 2006. From 'Oriori' to the Everly Brothers: Observations on the music of Nukumanu. Journal of the Polynesian Society 115(4): 365-381.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress or linguistic tone. Ethnomusicology article (Feinberg's 1984 Nukumanu fieldwork, Johnstone's musical analysis). Language content is segmental/orthographic only: p.365 'There is no published Nukumanu lexicon or dictionary'; p.373 in song, 'vowels shift so that, for example, an /a/ is pronounced as /o/'; p.374 n.8 no o/a possessive distinction; p.376 n.4 'Nukumanu has no glottal stop'; p.380 n.5 '/r/ and /l/ are not phonemically distinct on Nukumanu'. 'Tone'/'pitch'/'rhythm'/'tempo' occur only in the musical sense (two-pitch melodies, whole-tone descent, 'flat, straight t…

sources.citation: Feinberg, Richard (compiler and editor), with Tim Bayliss-Smith, Cato Berg, Joseph Finney, Janet Dixon Keller, Patrick V. Kirch, Rolf Kuschel, Judith Macdonald, Torben Monberg and Richard Moyle. 2005. A Polynesian Outlier Bibliography. Canberra: Australian National University, AnthroGlobe online bibliographies (coombs.anu.edu.au/Biblio/; site gone, Internet Archive copy 2008-07-27).
sources.note: Bibliography only. Its NUKUMANU section lists Bassett 1969, Bourke & Betitis 2003, Chinnery 1925, Elder 2001, Feinberg 1985 (Bikmaus 6(1):89-100), 1986a (Pacific Studies 9(3)), 1986b (Ethnology 25(4)), 1988, 1989, 1990, 1995, Feinberg & George 2005, O'Collins 1990, Parkinson 1897, 1898, 1907, 1986, Sarfert & Damm 1929 (2 vols), Shapiro 1932-33/1932/1933, Wankowski 1979, Willis & Booth 1968 - no grammar, phonology, dictionary or linguistic article on Nukumanu, confirming (as of 2005, from the specialist side) that no descriptive linguistic source exists beyond Ray/Friederici, Sarfert & Damm's…

sources.citation: Nukumanu New Testament (Wycliffe Bible Translators / Isles of the Sea, 2020) and any accompanying Nukumanu orthography statement or spelling guide by the Tasman translation committee (N. Daams, S. Andersen; cf. Te kkai te Ista 2003).
sources.note: Only recent published Nukumanu-language material; an orthography guide, if one was produced, would state how stress/length are treated.

sources.citation: Parkinson, R. 1986 [1897]. Ethnography of Ontong Java and Tasman Islands with remarks re: the Marqueen and Abgarris Islands. Translated by Rose S. Hartmann; introduced and annotated by Richard Feinberg. Pacific Studies 9(3): 1-31.
sources.note: No phonology content beyond spelling conventions for place names and a handful of Nukumanu lexical forms with doubled vowels/consonants; nothing on stress, accent or tone. Parkinson's own 'Sprache' passage (already read in the 1897 original) is translated without the vocabulary tables.

sources.citation: Lincoln, Peter C. 1976. Austronesian languages: Bougainville Province (pp. 419-439) and History of research in Austronesian languages: Bougainville Province (pp. 197-222). In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology for Nukumanu: sec. 4.4.9.2 says Nukuria, Takuu and Nukumanu 'are distinct speech varieties which are mutually intelligible or nearly so'; the research-history chapter refers readers to Pawley 1967, Biggs 1971, Elbert 1965 (Takuu sound correspondences) and Ray; only orthographic remark is that 'Takuu geminate stops (Elbert 1965)' trouble spellers.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1919/1920. The Polynesian languages in Melanesia. Anthropos 14-15: 46-96.
sources.note: Nukumanu (no. 5) represented only by Friederici MS words/numerals; Orthography section (p.57) merely notes Friederici 'marked the vowels and accents according to the Alphabet of Lepsius'; no stress rule for any northern Outlier.

sources.citation: Thilenius, G. 1902 [Nova Acta Bd. 80, 1903]. Ethnographische Ergebnisse aus Melanesien, I. Theil: Reisebericht; die polynesischen Inseln an der Ostgrenze Melanesiens. Nova Acta Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. 80(1).
sources.note: Nukumanu mentioned only ethnographically ('sprechen polynesisch'); the footnote p.84 'die Betonung von der samoanischen nicht abweicht' is attached to the 'Wortverzeichniss aus der Sprache von Nuguria' (nuku1259), not Nukumanu.

sources.citation: Parkinson, R. 1897. Zur Ethnographie der Ongtong Java- und Tasman-Inseln. Internationales Archiv fuer Ethnographie 10: 104-118, 137-151.
sources.note: 'Sprache' (pp.146-147): language of Ongtong Java/Tasman closest to Samoan, traders learn the 'Abweichungen in der Aussprache' in weeks; comparative word list (Samoa/Abgarris/Ongtong Java); nothing on Betonung.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Blust & Gray (eds), ABVD language 1654 Nukumanu; and ASJP list NUKUMANU (derived from it).
sources.note: Word lists only; no prosodic information.

sources.citation: Moyle, Richard M. 2011. Takuu Grammar and Dictionary: A Polynesian language of the South Pacific. Pacific Linguistics 634. Canberra: ANU.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6516.Z5 M69 2011)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6516.Z5 M69 2011
sources.note: Full grammar of the closest sister language (Takuu, reportedly mutually intelligible with Nukumanu); its stress section is the nearest available proxy and Moyle comments on Nukumanu-Takuu relations; would not itself qualify for nuku1258 but frames what to expect.
